turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): sorry doctor, we're late. the malahide road was a car park and then I couldn't get a space.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): you're grand. sit in there. no harm done.
[SEG0003] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): thanks a million. this is aoife, she's just gone six, and niamh minds her after school.
[SEG0004] person_3 (CAREGIVER): hiya doctor. she nodded off in the car, the heat of it.
[SEG0005] person_2 (DOCTOR): mm. so what brought ye down today.
[SEG0006] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): well it was the school that spooked us, if I'm honest. a girl in the class, saoirse, her mam rang to say she's got the measles.
[SEG0007] person_2 (DOCTOR): right. the classmate. and how is aoife in herself.
[SEG0008] person_4 (PATIENT): just spots. it's nothing.
[SEG0009] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): it is not nothing. she's come out in spots on her face and down her front, and she's been warm.
[SEG0010] person_2 (DOCTOR): ok, let me say it back. spots on the face and front, and a temperature, and ye're here because of the measles in school. when did the spots start.
[SEG0011] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): umm I can't put a day on it. since tuesday, or maybe the weekend, or after the school play. sometime last week, I don't know.
[SEG0012] person_3 (CAREGIVER): I thought I saw a bit of it monday at collection. or tuesday. the days run into each other.
[SEG0013] person_2 (DOCTOR): so nobody can date the start. the rash in measles tends to come a few days into it, but I can't count the days without a start. the warmth, has she had a real fever.
[SEG0014] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): yeah she was roasting yesterday. the thermometer at home said thirty eight point something. today she's a bit cooler but still warm, like.
[SEG0015] person_2 (DOCTOR): we'll measure it here. any cough, or trouble with her breathing.
[SEG0016] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): err. a tiny cough maybe yesterday. or she was just clearing her throat. I'm not sure, really.
[SEG0017] person_2 (DOCTOR): mixed answer, so I won't call it a cough for definite. anything with the tummy. vomiting, or diarrhoea.
[SEG0018] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): no. no vomiting and no diarrhoea. she's eating her yoghurt grand.
[SEG0019] person_2 (DOCTOR): and the eyes, the ears, the throat. any redness or soreness.
[SEG0020] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): no. eyes are clear, she hasn't been at her ears, throat's grand.
[SEG0021] person_2 (DOCTOR): is the rash itchy at all.
[SEG0022] person_4 (PATIENT): no. not itchy.
[SEG0023] person_3 (CAREGIVER): she was scratching like mad at breakfast, all over her belly.
[SEG0024] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): she does, when she thinks you're not looking. I'd say it is itchy.
[SEG0025] person_2 (DOCTOR): right, so aoife says not itchy and the two of ye say it is. I'll mark that as not agreed. any medicine ye've given.
[SEG0026] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): just calpoll. the six plus one. five mil, four times in the day, by mouth, for the fever.
[SEG0027] person_2 (DOCTOR): five mil of calpol six plus is two hundred and fifty milligram, up to four times a day. did she get one this morning.
[SEG0028] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): yeah, around eight, she swallowed it grand.
[SEG0029] person_2 (DOCTOR): what about vaccines. the mmr especially.
[SEG0030] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): oh. I think she had them. the red book is at home on the shelf. she might have missed the second dose when we moved, or maybe not, I honestly can't remember.
[SEG0031] person_2 (DOCTOR): grand, that's vague, bring the book next time. aoife, can I look at the spots. shirt up a small bit.
[SEG0032] person_4 (PATIENT): ok. that tickles.

[SEG0033] person_2 (DOCTOR): there's a red blotchy rash on the face, the chest and the tummy, and it fades when I press it. inside the cheeks I don't see any little white spots, and the chest is clear. pulse is a hundred and twelve, temperature now is thirty eight point four. oxygen is ninety eight percent.

[SEG0034] person_2 (DOCTOR): summing up then. rash and fever, classmate with measles, vaccines unclear, we can't date the start, cough not clear, itch not agreed. I'm not calling it measles for definite. it may be measles, or it may just be a viral rash, so we'll mind it as possible measles until proven otherwise.
[SEG0035] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): do we need a tablet, or a blood test or something.

[SEG0036] person_2 (DOCTOR): no new medicine. keep the calpol, five mil up to four times a day, if she's warm or uncomfortable. I'll notify public health this afternoon, and I'll request an oral fluid swab for measles. keep her off school, at home, away from babies and anyone pregnant, until public health tells ye otherwise.
[SEG0037] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): and do I ring the school.
[SEG0038] person_2 (DOCTOR): yes, tell them she's off and that public health are notified. I'll see ye back here in three days, friday, swab result or not.
[SEG0039] person_3 (CAREGIVER): friday, yeah we can do that.
[SEG0040] person_2 (DOCTOR): and if she gets hard to wake, or the breathing goes off, or the fever goes over forty, go straight to the emergency department. not the late chemist.
[SEG0041] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): god. ok. over forty, hospital.
[SEG0042] person_4 (PATIENT): can I get a sticker.
[SEG0043] person_2 (DOCTOR): you can. mind yourself, aoife.

Go to emergency if hard to wake, breathing worsens, or fever goes over 40
Bring the vaccination record next time

spec.situation: Parents of a child with rash and fever after a classmate had measles; vaccination status vague; doctor examines, counts days, plans notification and isolation advice.

traps.happens: The doctor asks only two to four review-of-systems questions (for example fever, weight, cough). Several other body systems are never asked about. One of the asked questions gets a vague or mixed answer.
traps.label_rule: negative_findings / review_of_systems ONLY for items the doctor actually asked AND the patient answered, evidence = that question and answer. Never add review-of-systems entries for systems nobody asked about, and never cite an unrelated turn (for example a turn about tiredness) for a system review.

traps.happens: The conversation OPENS with a remark, joke, apology for being late, small talk, or a trigger event (a relative's diagnosis, a neighbour's advice, the receptionist's note) BEFORE the real reason is stated. The patient states the real concern a few turns later.
traps.label_rule: chief_complaint is the real concern in a short phrase in the patient's wording (e.g. 'worried about diabetes', 'voice gets tired'). NOT the opening remark, the joke or the trigger (the relative's illness goes into family_history only if it is a relative's condition said as such).

features: spoken_numbers: doses, vitals and durations are spoken as words or sloppy speech ('a hundred and two point five', 'one-forty over ninety', 'five-ish years', 'twenty milligram'); the label writes them normally (102.5, 140/90, 20 mg) and does not turn vague ones into exact ones.
vague_dates: the patient cannot date things ('since Diwali or after', 'last winter, or the one before'); no invented date; a date_uncertain item.

bad.reason: After-school childminder is stated, but reported_by is caregiver/family intro, not family_member speaking for the fact.
bad.text: living (description=Childminder minds her after school, status=current, reported_by=family_member)

bad.reason: Uncertain cough reported, but doctor declines to call it a cough definite; current status not established.

omissions.text: Exposure history missing: a girl in her class (Saoirse) has measles, which prompted the visit.
Possible incomplete MMR vaccination history: family member thinks she had the MMRs but cannot remember, and she might have missed the second dose when they moved.
Home fever detail missing: yesterday she was 'roasting' and thermometer at home read 38 point something; today a bit cooler but still warm.
Negative finding not recorded: no trouble with breathing was asked and answered.

Medication detail recorded incompletely/wrongly: Calpol was specified as 'Calpol six plus one' / 'Calpol six plus'; doctor stated 5 mL equals 250 mg, and last dose was given around 8 this morning and swallowed fine.
Assessment/plan detail missing: doctor is not calling it measles for definite but will manage it as possible measles until proven otherwise.
Follow-up timing detail missing: review is specifically on Friday, in three days, even if the swab result is not back.
Safety-net wording incompletely recorded: attend ED if breathing goes off (not just worsens).
